name: esposter
description: A nice and casual place for posting random things.
author: Jimmy Chen

scripts.lint: virrun -- oxlint --format=default --disable-nested-config && virrun -- eslint . && virrun -- pnpm -r --parallel run lint
scripts.lint:fix: virrun -- oxlint --format=default --fix --disable-nested-config && virrun -- eslint --fix . && virrun -- pnpm -r --parallel run lint:fix
scripts.lint:fix:packages: virrun -- oxlint --format=default --fix --disable-nested-config packages && virrun -- pnpm -r --filter "./packages/*" --parallel run lint:fix
scripts.lint:packages: virrun -- oxlint --format=default --disable-nested-config packages && virrun -- pnpm -r --filter "./packages/*" --parallel run lint
scripts.release: pnpm format:check && pnpm build:packages && pnpm lint:packages && pnpm typecheck:packages && pnpm test:packages && lerna publish --yes
scripts.typecheck: virrun -- tsc && virrun -- pnpm -r --parallel run typecheck

scriptsComments.bench:ci: Not a shorter `pnpm bench`, and never run in its place. `bench` is `pnpm -r --workspace-concurrency=1`: every member owning a bench, one at a time, rewriting the committed `*.bench.md` a developer diffs. The concurrency flag is load-bearing twice over, because parallel benches skew each other's numbers and because the `scripts` cold-build bench deletes each `packages/*/dist` out from under a concurrent member still loading its `vitest.config.ts`, which surfaces as `Failed to resolve entry for package`. This one is a bare `vitest bench --run` at the root: one process over every project's bench files at once, which measures nothing anybody should compare and proves only that they all still execute. That is what the Bench workflow wants, and it is a script so the workflow names one rather than restating the command. See the `bench` skill.
scriptsComments.build: A deviation taken on purpose: the bare name means the whole workspace in a pnpm, turbo or nx repo alike, and here it means the web app plus the libraries it imports, because Railway runs `pnpm build` as its default build command. That makes this name a deploy entrypoint rather than a developer convenience, and widening it would have every deploy build two bundles it never ships. One selector, derived rather than named: `--filter "@esposter/web..."` is the app and everything it imports, in topological order, so the app builds last and nothing here knows which libraries exist. No `virrun --` on it, for the reason the virrun adoption docs page gives. `build:packages` is a different set: every library rather than the ones this app imports, which is what CI caches and hands to the checks, and the coverage shards build the two apps whose bundles the suite asserts against. There is no `build:<app>` script — one app is `pnpm -C apps/<app> run build` at the call site, and a root script that only delegates there is a second definition of the same line. @TODO: restore `pnpm build:docs` to the chain when a bridge build grows the AST navigation API. TypeDoc exits 6 against the `typescript-native-bridge` alias, and `build` is what deploy runs, so the deploy would fail on documentation alone. `build:docs` stays as the probe. See the `build-docs` job in .github/workflows/CI.yaml.
